provenance.authored_by: independent AI agent (separate session, no access to the system under test)
provenance.method: I authored eight chat corpora from scratch around fixed themes, varying one profiled speaker's habits across corpora (message length, emoji, questions, thread-starting, reply timing, word choice) while keeping each corpus internally consistent. No implementation, threshold, or repository code was read; each label is what I would say as a careful human reader perusing the transcript with its timestamps. Bands were chosen per the given vocabulary, with insufficient_evidence reserved for the corpus whose profiled speaker wrote too little to judge vocabulary.
provenance.disclosure: corpora and labels are AI-authored and disclosed as such; no thresholds of any implementation were available to the author

h1_launch_night.summary: A chatty colleague unwinding after launch day: quick, playful, mostly statement-led lines with a light sprinkling of emoji.

Response length.why: Most of their messages run ten to twenty words with a few longer riffs; ordinary chat length, neither clipped nor essay-like.

Emoji usage.why: A smiley or grin appears in roughly one message in five across all three chats — present and habitual, but never dense.

Questions.why: Almost everything is a statement or a tease; over three conversations they ask only two direct questions (the banner typo, inviting priya).

Initiation.why: They opened only one of the three conversations — the morning-after check-in; the other two begin with my messages.

Reply latency.why: Every reply that actually answers lands one to three minutes after my message, evening or morning alike.

Vocabulary.why: Casual but varied everyday register with a few workplace turns ('support tag breakdown', 'version numbers'); nothing repetitive, nothing showy.

h2_two_cities.summary: A warm long-distance friend who plans in whole paragraphs, asks constantly, and never touches an emoji.

Response length.why: Nearly every message is a full reflection or mini-itinerary of twenty to fifty words, launched even as a conversation opener.

Emoji usage.why: Not a single emoji or emoticon appears anywhere in their messages across the three conversations.

Questions.why: The threads are laced with direct asks — prices, weekends, parking, the kettle, breakfast timing — usually two or three per exchange.

Initiation.why: All three conversations begin with them, each opening a new planning thread.

Reply latency.why: Answers arrive ten to twenty minutes after mine during the live exchanges — unhurried and steady, never instant, never left for hours.

Vocabulary.why: Wide, fluid phrasing throughout — 'unsupervised in a spreadsheet', 'operationally ready', 'argue about it over that breakfast' — with varied, precise word choice.

h3_burst_pipe.summary: A flatmate in full minimal mode: one-to-seven-word acknowledgements, hours of silence, no questions, no decoration.

Response length.why: Their turns are almost all one to six words ('k', 'done. hall light's dead too now', 'friday'), with only a couple of short-sentence exceptions.

Emoji usage.why: No emoji or emoticon appears in any of their messages.

Questions.why: They never ask a direct question; every prompt in the chat starts with me.

Initiation.why: All three conversations are opened by me; they only ever pick threads up.

Reply latency.why: The gap between my message and their answer is usually half an hour to four hours, with one answer arriving the next morning.

Vocabulary.why: Across all three chats they write only around ninety words in total, nearly all formulaic one- and two-word turns, so there is not enough text to judge range honestly.

h4_career_crossroads.summary: A mentee weighing a job offer in compact, thoughtful messages, asking a few deliberate questions and using one emoji in total.

Response length.why: Messages typically run fifteen to thirty-five words — substantial but compact, with the longest being a forty-word opener.

Emoji usage.why: Exactly one emoji appears, a single 🙂 in the closing good-natured message; everything else is plain text.

Questions.why: Three pointed questions punctuate the corpus — the brief's narrowness, what the firm sees, and the sign-by-friday deadline.

Initiation.why: They opened two of the three conversations; I began the post-interview follow-up thread myself.

Reply latency.why: Answers land within half an hour to about three hours, all same-day — measured but never overnight.

Vocabulary.why: Deliberate, precise diction — 'romanticise', 'rehearsed in a meeting room', 'sentiment is tired but the specifics are all there', 'post-mortems, not theatre'.

h5_trail_weekend.summary: The trip's engine: emoji-studded, exclamation-heavy bursts, fast volleys, route nerdery, and a habit of ending messages on a plan.

Response length.why: A mix of short bursts and occasional thirty-word route notes; on balance ordinary chat length rather than consistently long.

Emoji usage.why: One to three emoji appear in nearly all of their messages, used almost as punctuation (bikes, weather, grins, croissants, phones).

Questions.why: They are constantly polling — start times, water sources, tomas's knee, mara's number, arrival times — eight direct questions across the three chats.

Initiation.why: They start all three conversations, one per planning day.

Reply latency.why: Almost every reply comes one to three minutes after mine; it is the fastest rhythm in the whole set.

Vocabulary.why: Route-literate and varied — reservoir, gorge, switchback-free but gravel, brake pads, salt tablets, campervans — with inventive phrasing that never loops on standby words.

h6_mums_seventieth.summary: A sibling juggling party logistics in single-line texts sent hours apart, with sparse family-themed emoji and dry punchlines.

Response length.why: Nearly all of their messages are one line, rarely more than a dozen words, in both planning and joking.

Emoji usage.why: A smiley or a cake emoji recurs every few messages — sparse but clearly habitual rather than absent.

Questions.why: Three practical asks sit across the corpus — the guest list, dani's confirmation, and chasing the run sheet.

Initiation.why: They opened two of the three conversations (the hall-booking and the run-sheet check); I began the first.

Reply latency.why: Their answers typically arrive two to four hours later, and twice the conversation waits until the next day; the rare quick replies are the exception, not the rhythm.

Vocabulary.why: Ordinary family-and-logistics vocabulary with occasional dry turns — 'coronation', 'constitution', 'jinx' — neither impoverished nor adventurous.

h7_overdue_invoice.summary: A courteous freelancer chasing a late invoice in businesslike paragraphs, spelling terms out precisely and ending each thread on an agreement.

Response length.why: Messages usually run fifteen to thirty-five words, occasionally longer when setting out terms — professional paragraphs, not essays.

Emoji usage.why: No emoji or emoticon appears at any point in the three threads.

Questions.why: Statement-led throughout, but with five procedural questions — payment date, remittance advice, escalation route, portal status, the launch date.

Initiation.why: They start all three conversations: the first nudge, the follow-up check-in, and the next-phase terms.

Reply latency.why: Replies typically come within half an hour of an hour and a half, with one answer waiting nearly four hours; nothing overnight and nothing instant.

Vocabulary.why: Businesslike and consistent — remittance, reconciled, ledger, terms, escalation — clear and competent but not adventurous.

h8_book_club.summary: A bookish neighbour two doors down who reviews the novel in measured, image-rich paragraphs and never fires off a quick volley.

Response length.why: Most messages are two to four sentences of twenty to forty-five words, reading like spoken criticism written down.

Emoji usage.why: No emoji or emoticon appears anywhere in their messages.

Questions.why: They ask only one question in three conversations (whether the tense changes in part two); everything else is observation extended toward me.

Initiation.why: They opened two of the three conversations — the margin-page update and the finished-novel check-in; I began the first.

Reply latency.why: They never volley: the fastest reply is about forty minutes, most arrive after an hour or two, and several exchanges wait overnight until the next morning.

Vocabulary.why: Literary and wide-ranging — 'repetition itself', 'plot traffic', 'legible', 'reverence', 'prophecy', 'reallocation' — with almost no repeated pet phrases.
